"title": "GUIDEMOL: a Python graphical user interface for molecular descriptors based on RDKit",

"executive_summary": "GUIDEMOL is a Python graphical user interface (GUI) built on the RDKit chemoinformatics toolkit that allows users without programming skills to calculate molecular descriptors and 3D grid representations of molecular structures. The application is grounded in the QSPR/QSAR methodology, which relies on molecular descriptors as core inputs, and addresses a gap in accessible, teaching-oriented software for chemoinformatics. The GUI is constructed using tkinter, the standard Python interface to the Tcl/Tk GUI toolkit, and employs various widgets including buttons, checkbuttons, radiobuttons, entries, labels, and a scrollbar, all controlled by the grid geometry manager. Users can select input and output files through native look-and-feel dialog windows implemented with the tkinter.filedialog module, and a log file is created to register successful processing and failures for each molecule. The software generates 3D molecular models using the RDKit function MMFFOptimizeMolecule with the MMFF94 force field variant and a maximum of 5000 iterations, with options to remove metals, keep the largest fragment, or neutralize the molecule, and to add hydrogen atoms. For descriptor calculation, the interface provides access to several 3D descriptors available in the RDKit rdMolDescriptors module, including RDF, MORSE, WHIM, AUTOCORR3D, GETAWAY, PEOE_VSA, and SMR_VSA, as well as the exact molecular weight. Beyond descriptors, GUIDEMOL implements direct 3D representations of molecular structures through electrostatic potential grids or voxel encoding. The electrostatic potential at each grid cube is computed from partial atomic charges (Gasteiger or MMFF) using a Coulombic formula, while voxelization encodes atomic properties such as atomic number, partial charge, or contributions to molecular refractivity and logP using the Wildman-Crippen approach with a Gaussian decay function. The source code is released under the three-clause BSD license and is available on GitHub, allowing both commercial and non-commercial use and easy extension for other descriptors or tasks. A command-line interface (CLI) is also provided for the calculation of electrostatic potential and voxel grids, enabling batch processing without the GUI. The paper notes that some descriptor values may differ across runs or operating systems due to numerical sensitivity, and highlights the potential for these 3D representations to be processed by deep learning neural networks, including convolutional neural networks, for larger datasets. Overall, GUIDEMOL serves as a minimalist interface to routine chemoinformatics tasks, facilitating access to well-established descriptors and 3D representations for scientists and students in chemistry, biology, and material science education.",

summary.title: GUIDEMOL: a Python graphical user interface for molecular descriptors based on RDKit

The application is grounded in the QSPR/QSAR methodology, which relies on molecular descriptors as core inputs, and addresses a gap in accessible, teaching-oriented software for chemoinformatics. The GUI is constructed using tkinter, the standard Python interface to the Tcl/Tk GUI toolkit, and employs various widgets including buttons, checkbuttons, radiobuttons, entries, labels, and a scrollbar, all controlled by the grid geometry manager. Users can select input and output files through native look-and-feel dialog windows implemented with the tkinter.filedialog module, and a log file is created to register successful processing and failures for each molecule. The software generates 3D molecular models using the RDKit function MMFFOptimizeMolecule with the MMFF94 force field variant and a maximum of 5000 iterations, with options to remove metals, keep the largest fragment, or neutralize the molecule, and to add hydrogen atoms. For descriptor calculation, the interface provides access to several 3D descriptors available in the RDKit rdMolDescriptors module, including RDF, MORSE, WHIM, AUTOCORR3D, GETAWAY, PEOE_VSA, and SMR_VSA, as well as the exact molecular weight. Beyond descriptors, GUIDEMOL implements direct 3D representations of molecular structures through electrostatic potential grids or voxel encoding. The electrostatic potential at each grid cube is computed from partial atomic charges (Gasteiger or MMFF) using a Coulombic formula, while voxelization encodes atomic properties such as atomic number, partial charge, or contributions to molecular refractivity and logP using the Wildman-Crippen approach with a Gaussian decay function. The source code is released under the three-clause BSD license and is available on GitHub, allowing both commercial and non-commercial use and easy extension for other descriptors or tasks. A command-line interface (CLI) is also provided for the calculation of electrostatic potential and voxel grids, enabling batch processing without the GUI. The paper notes that some descriptor values may differ across runs or operating systems due to numerical sensitivity, and highlights the potential for these 3D representations to be processed by deep learning neural networks, including convolutional neural networks, for larger datasets. Overall, GUIDEMOL serves as a minimalist interface to routine chemoinformatics tasks, facilitating access to well-established descriptors and 3D representations for scientists and students in chemistry, biology, and material science education.
